Hypothesis to revise: TITLE: Two-round self-training: regenerating pseudo-masks from MVFA's own adapted features
SUMMARY: Train MVFA on label-restricted pseudo-masks from frozen CLIP features, then regenerate the pseudo-masks with the trained model's adapted segmentation features and retrain once.
HYPOTHESIS: A second round of pseudo-mask generation from MVFA's own adapted level-4 segmentation features raises pseudo-mask Dice against true masks by at least 8 points over round-1 pseudo-masks from frozen CLIP features, and the round-2 model recovers at least 5 points more of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: Superpixel snapping and DINOv2 propagation both import a better notion of image structure from outside MVFA, either raw intensity or a second backbone. The common explanation of their gain is that frozen CLIP features are a poor basis for localisation. MVFA's adapters are trained precisely to recalibrate CLIP features toward anomaly localisation (the paper's central claim), so after one round of training on noisy pseudo-masks the adapted features should separate lesion from normal tissue better than frozen CLIP features, and pseudo-masks regenerated from them should be cleaner. This self-training route uses the target method's own mechanism instead of an external prior, and image-level labels keep it anchored: regeneration is restricted to images labelled abnormal, which prevents the confirmation drift that unlabelled self-training suffers.
METHOD: 1) Round 1: make_pseudo_masks.py with frozen CLIP layer-24 features (label-restricted rule, 99th percentile on source validation); train MVFA with train_zero.py as usual. 2) Round 2: extract the trained model's adapted seg features at level 4 (output of seg_adapters[3] mixed residually) for normal and abnormal source training images; recompute normal-to-normal NN distances on source validation, threshold at the 99th percentile, and regenerate masks for abnormal images only. 3) Retrain from the CLIP initialisation (not from round 1) on the round-2 masks to avoid accumulating overfitting. 4) Stop after two rounds; a third round is an ablation. Hyper-parameters as MVFA; selection on source validation against the current round's pseudo-masks.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; round 1; round 2; round 3 (ablation); masks removed from all 3 masked sources and the image-only datasets added as pseudo-mask sources. Ablation: round 2 without label restriction (regenerate on all images). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per round, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if round-2 pseudo-mask Dice does not exceed round 1 by 8 points or the round-2 model does not improve pixel AUROC by 5 points of recovered gain.
